styles.name: Swiss Editorial / The Public Ledger
styles.thesis: Make the subject legible through a visible ordering system: a publication whose navigation, captions and arguments share one precise alignment, with asymmetry doing the expressive work.
composition: Use a twelve-track wide grid: a two-track contents rail, a six-track reading column and a four-track evidence field. Align headings, image edges and rules to these tracks rather than centering every section.
Open with the actual editorial question, a compact publication/date line and one subject artifact; let the title occupy a deliberately unequal share of the page.
Alternate a long reading run with one full-grid diagram or photograph. Use rules to mark changes of topic, not boxes around every paragraph.
Keep section anchors and descriptive contents labels stable; an active marker follows the section without moving the contents list.
styles.typography: Start with a workmanlike grotesk with distinguishable I/l/1 and a real italic; use weight, size and alignment before a second family. Body 1–1.125rem at about 62ch; titles may jump to 5rem but captions remain readable. Rag-right prose, tabular figures for dates and a consistent caption baseline matter more than tight tracking. Basel's experimental lineage is not interchangeable with Zurich's rationalism.
styles.material: Flat ink, sharp crops, source-labeled diagrams and honest image captions. Commission a diagram of the actual subject instead of adding a Swiss-looking red circle.
styles.motion: A section indicator may move in a short transition; reading content appears immediately. No staggered paragraph entrances. Reduced motion switches the indicator without travel.
styles.interaction: Use ordinary anchor links for contents, a visible skip link and shareable section IDs. Back returns to the prior article or section without resetting reading position. Mark the current destination independently of accent color.
styles.mobile: Replace the side rail with a labeled contents disclosure before the article; keep the evidence field inline beside the argument it supports. Collapse to one reading column, preserve captions and never squeeze body type to retain the desktop grid.
styles.use_when: The work has a strong argument, archive, public record or information hierarchy worth exposing; a team can supply real editorial material.
styles.avoid_when: The grid becomes a fetish that separates labels from their content, or a playful established identity would be erased by institutional restraint.
styles.signature: A continuous alignment line links the title, section index and evidence captions: order is both the visual motif and the reading tool.

styles.name: Bauhaus Play / The Working Toy
styles.thesis: Explain the product by assembling it: a small vocabulary of useful geometric parts creates both a memorable picture and a clear route into the work.
composition: Divide the opening into a large working demonstration and a narrow instruction strip; the demonstration must depict a real mechanism or relationship.
Choose three primitive shapes and assign each a persistent job, such as source, transformation and result. Do not scatter unassigned triangles as background confetti.
Follow the demonstration with a horizontal sequence of cause, action and output, then a concrete start point; vary scale and orientation around a stable text baseline.
Use offset blocks and deliberate negative space, but keep the navigation in a predictable, unrotated band.
styles.typography: Use a geometric or humanist sans with an open lowercase and a comfortable text weight. Reserve circular or constructed letterforms for a short title or diagram labels; do not impose a historical display face on form instructions. Body around 1.0625rem, strong sentence-case verbs, two or three distinct sizes rather than many nearly equal ones.
styles.material: Cut-paper silhouettes or original vector parts based on the product's actual modules. Additional vermilion or yellow can identify diagram categories, with dark labels and a redundant legend. Bauhaus was a varied school and workshop, not a mandatory primary-color kit.
styles.motion: Animate one assembly on explicit activation; parts connect to reveal a real output. Provide a static assembled frame, replay control and reduced-motion cross-state replacement.
styles.interaction: Each operable shape has a text equivalent and a conventional control. Keyboard users can select the same inputs as drag users; the final action is named for its result, not 'Explore magic'.
styles.mobile: Turn the large assembly into a vertical three-stage demonstration; let the text precede each manipulated object. Use tap/select alternatives instead of requiring precision dragging.
styles.use_when: The offering has modular parts, a teachable transformation or an invitation to experiment that can be demonstrated truthfully.
styles.avoid_when: Geometry is only decoration, the task is an urgent repetitive operation, or the interaction requires manipulating shapes before finding basic information.
styles.signature: The same three parts appear in the explanation, the control affordances and the resulting artifact, making play a way to understand the system.

styles.name: Editorial Luxe / The Object Monograph
styles.thesis: Treat the object as worthy of close attention, then make the practical buying or reading decision unusually plain; value comes from specificity and pacing, not a luxury costume.
composition: Begin with one large object study and a title/edition block on unequal columns, with price or availability visible when commerce is the job.
Sequence overview, material detail, maker/process and practical specifications like a short monograph. Alternate close crops and generous contextual images rather than repeating product cards.
Give specifications an aligned ledger and the transaction a calm, separate action zone; keep delivery, returns and variant information near the decision.
Provide a text index or collection route alongside any visual shelf so a visitor need not decode a sculptural navigation device.
styles.typography: Pair a moderately contrasted reading serif with a quiet sans for price, format and controls. Keep the serif robust at small sizes and reserve fine hairlines for large titles. Try 1.125rem/1.6 prose at 56–64ch; captions remain close to their images. No obligatory spaced-out uppercase or unreadably thin gray labels.
styles.material: Original photography or renders that disclose scale, construction and detail; consistent lighting plus one deliberate change of crop. A missing product image is an asset problem, not an excuse for ornamental gradients.
styles.motion: A user-controlled object rotation or detail dissolve can support inspection; keep price and action stationary. Reduced motion uses still angles with labeled next/previous controls.
styles.interaction: Collection, detail and purchase are real destinations. Variants visibly change the selected option, available stock and image; unavailable choices explain why. Any sticky purchase band must not cover focused content.
styles.mobile: Bring name, essential object view, price and availability together before the long essay. Replace hover-only image details with labeled controls; use inline chapter links rather than a miniature desktop shelf.
styles.use_when: Real objects, editions, hospitality details or bodies of work justify patient looking and have accurate practical information.
styles.avoid_when: Stock photography is all that exists, the task is rapid multi-item comparison, or atmosphere conceals cost and restrictions.
styles.signature: A close-up detail and its exact specification share a spread, joining emotional attention to practical evidence.

styles.name: Neo-Brutalist / The Open Noticeboard
styles.thesis: Put the terms, contents and available actions on the surface; graphic bluntness should make the interface more candid, not more hostile.
composition: Use a strong page perimeter, a large factual heading and a dense but ordered index of entries; let one deliberately oversized entry break the rhythm.
Separate regions with ink rules and one offset panel rather than wrapping every item in a drop-shadow card.
Make a native-looking list or table the functional center, with metadata aligned across entries and useful descriptions visible before hover.
Place constraints, costs or status in the same field as the action instead of hiding them in a polished secondary screen.
styles.typography: Use a sturdy sans or a deliberately ordinary browser family at generous sizes; one expressive display face may interrupt the index. Dense labels still need normal case, distinguishable characters and sensible line length. Monospace belongs to IDs or actual code, not every sentence.
styles.material: Flat saturated fields, visible borders and rough-but-authored original image cuts. The exposed structure is intentional; broken images, random rotations and fake browser errors are not the concept.
styles.motion: Hard state changes or a short displacement on activation reinforce the physical button. Do not shake the page, flash backgrounds or require a custom cursor. Reduced motion retains border and fill feedback.
styles.interaction: Underlined destinations remain distinguishable from push buttons. Use conspicuous focus distinct from the thick decorative border, normal browser history and reversible filters. A loud visual language does not excuse surprise navigation.
styles.mobile: Stack metadata under each item with explicit field labels. Preserve comfortable hit regions and prevent thick borders or oversized headings from causing horizontal overflow.
styles.use_when: Candor, independent publishing, direct catalog browsing or a deliberately unvarnished brand supports the content and audience.
styles.avoid_when: Aggression would undermine the task, the existing brand has a different authority, or visual roughness is being used to excuse unfinished states.
styles.signature: An oversized, fully functional index entry behaves like a public notice: unmistakable content, unmistakable action.

styles.name: Organic Humanist / The Field Companion
styles.thesis: Build familiarity through an identifiable hand, humane language and the rhythm of a real process; warmth should survive the form, error and receipt, not end at the illustration.
composition: Open with a concrete human scene or artifact beside the task statement, not a generic smiling portrait and a promise of transformation.
Alternate broad illustrated fields with compact, clearly bounded work areas. Keep inputs on stable flat surfaces and let organic forms live around, not behind, their labels.
Use a recurring process line or motif to connect stages; each stage has a plain heading, relevant evidence and a next action.
Group related details through proximity and small changes of tint; reserve outlines for actual controls and important boundaries.
styles.typography: Choose a humanist sans with open counters and comfortable punctuation, optionally paired with a warm reading serif. Give long instructions about 60ch and body text 1.0625–1.125rem. Handwriting may annotate a drawing, never carry required instructions or error recovery.
styles.material: Commission a small family of subject-specific drawings, photographed materials or process marks. Define stroke, crop and texture rules; do not collage unrelated stock illustrations. Cultural sources inform named techniques, not a generic 'ethnic' mood.
styles.motion: Use a gentle change of contour or line completion at a meaningful milestone, once per action. No perpetual breathing on task controls; reduced motion uses the completed motif and explicit status text.
styles.interaction: Forms explain what is needed before submission, preserve entries on error and show the exact next step. Keep assistance reachable without abandoning the task; success language confirms an actual saved result.
styles.mobile: Crop drawings to a deliberate detail instead of shrinking them to badges. Place instructions next to each input, retain large labels and avoid ornamental curves that consume the first screen.
styles.use_when: A process benefits from reassurance, patient explanation or a recognizable maker's voice, with assets tied to the real subject.
styles.avoid_when: Softness masks uncertainty or seriousness, ornamental illustration adds no understanding, or the audience needs maximum comparison density.
styles.signature: One process motif becomes both a chapter connector and a truthful completion marker, joining character with orientation.

styles.name: Kinetic Poster / The Live Programme
styles.thesis: Let an event's organizing idea act on type and image, while dates, locations and booking remain as dependable as a printed programme.
composition: Make the opening an authored poster with a fixed practical strip for date, place and booking; the expressive title is not the navigation.
Derive one deformation, repetition or cut from the subject's physical process and carry it into chapter transitions, not every component.
Follow the poster with a program ledger organized by day or venue, with filters that reflect how attendees plan a visit.
Give individual events shareable detail routes and a consistent return to the selected program view.
styles.typography: Use one variable or condensed display family for the poster and a stable, open text face for schedule rows. Expressive line breaks can be fixed for a title; dates and locations must wrap naturally. Optical size and width changes must not shift focused controls.
styles.material: Author light studies, scans, collage or typography from the actual medium of the event. Pentagram's BFI account suggests a method—physical projection becoming identity—not permission to copy its letters, palette or footage.
styles.motion: A short, pausable title study can reveal the graphic premise; the date and action are present from frame one. No scroll hijacking, strobe or mandatory intro. Reduced motion opens on the designed final still.
styles.interaction: Program filters expose selected values and result counts; 'Book [event]' identifies the destination. Keep an explicit schedule list even if an experimental spatial browse is offered.
styles.mobile: Art-direct a portrait poster rather than scaling the landscape composition. Put date/place and booking before the motion field; collapse filters into a labeled sheet while keeping active selections visible outside it.
styles.use_when: A campaign, event or cultural program has a concrete organizing idea and genuinely strong typographic or moving-image assets.
styles.avoid_when: The program cannot be found without watching, animation pushes essential information away, or the task is a frequently repeated operation.
styles.signature: A physical transformation of the subject becomes a single typographic event, then resolves into a clear program index.

styles.name: Cinematic Gallery / The Screening Room
styles.thesis: Give each work a room and a duration without making the visitor surrender control; the image leads, but orientation never disappears.
composition: Open on one decisive still with work title, medium and an obvious project index. Establish scale through the work, not an unrelated atmospheric video.
Sequence overview, detail and context as distinct image ratios, with captions at predictable edges and useful negative space between works.
Offer a compact text index alongside the immersive mode, including title, year and category where those help selection.
End each project with credits, next work and an index return; do not strand the viewer in a fullscreen cul-de-sac.
styles.typography: Use restrained screen-readable captions and one expressive title treatment derived from the work. Body text about 1.0625rem at 55–65ch on an opaque reading plane. Captions must not disappear against changing images; serif or sans follows the work rather than a rule that dark galleries need one particular face.
styles.material: Use licensed or original high-quality stills with an explicit crop, poster frame and descriptive text alternative. Serve appropriately sized images; provide credits. Fullscreen video and WebGL are optional enhancements, not prerequisites to seeing the portfolio.
styles.motion: Use user-initiated cuts or dissolves between works and a real pause/mute path for media. Avoid heavy parallax and forced horizontal scroll. Reduced motion uses stills and direct changes with all captions intact.
styles.interaction: Previous/next controls have names and visible position. Each work has a URL; browser Back exits detail to the previous collection state. Escape exits any fullscreen overlay and returns focus to its opener.
styles.mobile: Prefer a vertical sequence of stills and concise captions. Use swipe only as an additional input to visible controls; keep project index and contact reachable without traversing every image.
styles.use_when: The work itself has visual depth, strong imagery and meaningful sequencing; atmosphere supports looking rather than compensating for absent content.
styles.avoid_when: Most users need rapid feature comparison, bandwidth is constrained with no image fallback, or experimental navigation hides the actual work.
styles.signature: A persistent small index holds the room together while the scale and rhythm of the images change dramatically.

styles.name: Quiet Craft / The Maker's Record
styles.thesis: Let the evidence of making carry the identity: patient spacing, precise descriptions and close material observation replace both sterile minimalism and sentimental rustic decoration.
composition: Begin with an honest workshop artifact or detail study, a short factual statement and the next useful destination.
Organize the page as a sequence of material, process, finished object and care; vary image scale while keeping text on a dependable measure.
Use thin dividers and caption alignment for grouping; let one generous pause separate chapters instead of putting every fragment in a box.
Give dimensions, maintenance, availability and ordering conditions a straightforward list near the relevant object.
styles.typography: Choose a bookish serif or carefully proportioned humanist sans; use real italics for specimen notes and an ordinary sans for controls if needed. Body 1.125rem with generous leading, captions no smaller than their actual reading context allows. Test ink-like colors against the real canvas; low contrast is not quietness.
styles.material: Photograph grain, joinery, wear or fabrication with consistent light; include scale and imperfect real details. Texture belongs in images or a low-cost surface treatment, never as an overlay that dirties required text.
styles.motion: Small disclosure changes and an optional before/after material study suffice. No simulated inertia for normal scrolling. Reduced motion loses no process explanation.
styles.interaction: Give care notes, dimensions and ordering their own readable headings. An inquiry form asks only for information needed to answer; show confirmation and a truthful response expectation if known, not invented urgency.
styles.mobile: Maintain a comfortable reading column with intentional image crops; bring dimensions and cost close to the action. Do not leave enormous desktop blank spaces between a label and its value.
styles.use_when: Process, authorship, maintenance or material honesty is a real part of the offering and can be shown specifically.
styles.avoid_when: 'Craft' is an invented narrative, evidence is absent, or the interface needs dense repeated operations rather than patient inspection.
styles.signature: A material close-up is paired with a precise making or care note: the visual detail earns the prose beside it.

styles.name: Deco Geometric / The Modern Marquee
styles.thesis: Create ceremony through proportion, repeated geometry and a clear central axis, while keeping practical information in a crisp contemporary booking or catalog system.
composition: Frame one opening subject with a stepped perimeter or repeated arch derived from its architecture; use a strong central axis without centering long paragraphs.
Limit ornamental geometry to chapter gates, an identity mark and one navigation detail. Let the information areas use straightforward aligned columns.
Sequence invitation, venue/object detail, practical options and reservation; repeat a proportional interval rather than the same decorative card.
Use a compact labeled index and explicit availability or session lists beneath the ceremonial opening.
styles.typography: Keep a geometric display face for short titles and pair it with a robust text face. Verify ambiguous letterforms in names and dates. Use letter spacing selectively at display scale, not as an automatic treatment for every button or caption; body remains left-aligned around 58ch.
styles.material: Draw original geometry from the subject's structural details, with flat brass-like color rather than unreadable metallic text. Art Deco is a heterogeneous movement with complex global borrowings; do not recycle decontextualized cultural motifs as a luxury shorthand.
styles.motion: A single frame may open like a proscenium, with the contents already available. Controls respond directly, without theatrical waiting. Reduced motion shows the open frame from the start.
styles.interaction: Reservation dates, quantities and costs use familiar inputs with visible selected states. An elegant frame must not constrain form labels or hide the cancellation route. Link labels name destinations rather than decorative symbols.
styles.mobile: Keep one simplified geometric border and remove secondary ornament. Stack practical options in reading order; large display text may wrap, but dates, prices and form labels cannot be clipped to preserve symmetry.
styles.use_when: A real venue, edition or event supports a ceremonial entrance and there is subject-specific architectural or decorative material.
styles.avoid_when: Historical ornament would be a costume without context, the established identity conflicts, or ceremony adds friction to a routine task.
styles.signature: A subject-derived stepped frame recurs as a chapter gate and a restrained current-location marker.

styles.name: Retro-Future / The Useful Instrument
styles.thesis: Borrow the clarity and tactility of an imagined instrument, not the illegibility of a film prop; every visible signal must refer to something real.
composition: Build a stable instrument frame around one live work area: input on one side, result in the center, provenance and status on the other.
Use a restrained module boundary and a small amount of repeated calibration geometry to establish rhythm; avoid coating every region in neon.
Place actual operating state and last-update information near the result. Remove fake waveforms, arbitrary coordinates and decorative uptime counters.
Give the frame a conventional project/menu route and a visible way back from deep settings.
styles.typography: Pair a readable technical sans with monospace only for real values, code or aligned identifiers. Distinguish zero/O and one/l in critical data. Body starts around 1rem; display numerals may be large, but never use all-caps microtext as the only explanation.
styles.material: Original instrument diagrams, shallow bevels or a limited phosphor-like accent can identify editable vs read-only regions. CRT scanlines, grain and chromatic aberration stay off required information and are dispensable.
styles.motion: Animate a real state transition or measured signal only when it changes. Provide pause for continuously updating displays and no flashing terminal theatrics. Reduced motion keeps numerical and textual updates without animated sweeps.
styles.interaction: Controls expose units, range and current value. Every dial has a keyboard-operable numeric alternative; apply/reset are explicit and failures retain the last valid result with a stale marker.
styles.mobile: Turn the instrument into task, result and details in that order. Replace tiny dials with labeled inputs; keep status near the result and make horizontally dense logs an explicitly labeled scroll region.
styles.use_when: The product genuinely measures, transforms, simulates or controls something and the instrument metaphor clarifies its operation.
styles.avoid_when: The design needs fictitious telemetry to feel futuristic, or a skin of gauges obscures a simple content or purchasing task.
styles.signature: An editable input and a traceable result share one calibration spine, connecting the imagined object to a real operation.

styles.name: Systemic Product / The Working Desk
styles.thesis: Make the work scene immediately understandable: stable navigation establishes scope, a clear workspace carries the task and restrained personality comes from exact content and behavior rather than copied SaaS chrome.
composition: Separate organization/project scope from the local view. Use a labeled persistent rail for stable destinations and a compact page header for the current object and its actions.
Choose a primary work form—queue, board, calendar, editor or split view—from the job rather than defaulting to a metric dashboard.
Put selection-dependent actions next to the selected work and keep global creation distinct. An optional inspector may explain an object without squeezing the main task below a useful width.
Use row grouping, section headings and whitespace before nested cards; disclose secondary metadata without removing essential comparison fields.
styles.typography: Use a UI family that holds labels, mixed scripts, numerals and punctuation at practical sizes. Set a clear title/body/label/data hierarchy, tabular figures where alignment matters and readable secondary text. Compact mode is a deliberate user/task choice, not a reason to shrink every control.
styles.material: Quiet opaque layers, crisp separators and a small subject-specific illustration only where it helps first use or explanation. Shadows identify actual overlays; blur and glass are optional only if focus and contrast remain reliable.
styles.motion: Use short transitions to explain selection, panel opening and saved status. Never animate the whole queue on refresh; reduced motion keeps selection and status changes immediate.
styles.interaction: Real routes, explicit current project, visible local filters and preserved Back/Forward state are primary. Offer keyboard shortcuts as accelerators with discoverable buttons; maintain focus across edits and provide undo for reversible actions. Do not infer that Linear's visual refresh solved its deeper navigation issues.
styles.mobile: Change the split view into list/detail routes with a labeled return, persist filters and scroll position, and expose essential global destinations in a compact labeled navigation. A rail shrunk to unexplained icons is not an adaptation.
styles.use_when: People return to perform specific operations and need stable scope, state and recovery across many views.
styles.avoid_when: The surface is an immersive portfolio, the task does not justify persistent chrome, or a visual redesign is being substituted for an unresolved information architecture.
styles.signature: The selected object, current scope and next useful action form one unmistakable working triangle across all views.

styles.name: Data Atelier / The Evidence Bench
styles.thesis: Put the question and its evidence in the same visual field; analytical craft comes from meaningful comparison, traceable values and honest uncertainty, not a dashboard of impressive-looking numbers.
composition: Open with the question, data scope and time range, followed by the single comparison that can answer it. Do not lead with arbitrary KPI tiles.
Align a chart, an explanatory annotation and a supporting table on a shared measure; give the table enough width for actual comparison.
Use a persistent filter strip with active values, reset and clear units. Show missing or excluded observations beside the result rather than in a hidden footnote.
Separate exploration from export or saved reports, and keep source/provenance reachable from the result itself.
styles.typography: Use a clear sans for annotations and tabular numerals for aligned values; a reading serif may carry the analytical argument. Prefer direct labels over tiny legends. Right-align comparable quantities, show units in headers and choose precision from measurement quality rather than a uniform decimal count.
styles.material: Original charts of real or clearly labeled illustrative data. Semantic series colors, direct annotations and restrained rules expose comparison; no pseudo-scientific grid wallpaper, unexplained sparklines or fabricated performance metrics.
styles.motion: Transition only when it clarifies a change in data scope; show updating and stale states separately. Pause live feeds on demand. Reduced motion replaces chart interpolation with direct redraw and a textual result summary.
styles.interaction: Sorting controls name the column and expose direction; selection is distinct from row navigation. Show filtered result counts and zero-result recovery. Provide an accessible table or summary for charts; tooltips cannot contain the only available value.
styles.mobile: Prioritize the analytical question and key comparison, then let users choose columns or open row detail. Preserve a horizontally scrollable semantic table when comparison truly requires it; do not transform every data cell into a disconnected card.
styles.use_when: A decision depends on comparisons, scope and provenance; the underlying data and its limitations can be explained.
styles.avoid_when: The content has no analytical question, a metric display is merely decorative, or the data is too uncertain to support the implied precision.
styles.signature: Each major finding sits beside the exact comparison, units and source that permit a reader to challenge it.

styles.name: Wayfinding / The Legible Route
styles.thesis: Let people know where they are, what is available and how to recover; the visual identity grows out of a consistent route language, not a decorative map metaphor.
composition: State the current place or task as the page heading; give local choices a consistent region and show the parent destination when the hierarchy matters.
Group destinations by visitor intent or object, not the organization's internal departments. Give each route a short label and enough description to disambiguate.
For a flexible multi-session service, show a task ledger with truthful status and dependencies; for an obligatory sequence, use a step structure instead of a misleading freely navigable task list.
Use signs, numbering and route lines only when they encode actual hierarchy, sequence or state. Keep a clear completion or return destination at every terminal page.
styles.typography: Choose readable open forms and a generous distinction between destination, description and status. Test labels out of context: 'Manage' is insufficient without an object. Avoid uppercase paragraphs; give long place names room to wrap and make route numbers visually subordinate to their names.
styles.material: A small vocabulary of directional marks, region labels and contrast bands. Icons reinforce words; color does not independently define the route. This is an interpretation of signage discipline, not an attempt to reproduce a transit brand.
styles.motion: Keep location changes direct, with a stable header and purposeful focus destination. A progress line updates only after real completion. Reduced motion removes travel but preserves current-location and status feedback.
styles.interaction: Use semantic links, disclosure buttons for optional route groups and aria-current for the active page. Include direct entry, permission errors, unavailable destinations and Back/Forward in the route plan. Search supplements browse and never becomes the only way to reach core tasks.
styles.mobile: Retain destination names and route hierarchy; a contents disclosure or task sheet can replace the wide rail. Surface current location outside closed navigation. Fixed bars must not obscure keyboard focus or completion messages.
styles.use_when: The hard part is choosing a destination, understanding a service or resuming work across several visits and routes.
styles.avoid_when: A route diagram adds needless abstraction to a simple page, or a forced stepper prevents legitimate nonlinear work.
styles.signature: A stable location strip and a truthful task ledger make the next decision visible without requiring the visitor to remember the site map.

styles.name: Illustrated World / The Living Field Guide
styles.thesis: Give the subject its own visual ecology: a coherent cast of forms, places and marks makes information memorable without turning navigation into a guessing game.
composition: Open with an original scene whose focal element introduces the real subject, with a plain title and next step beside it.
Develop two scales: an overview environment for orientation and close specimen views for specific explanations. Reuse motifs by meaning rather than repeating random stickers.
Place long text and forms in calm, predictable reading clearings; the scene's contour must not dictate an erratic text measure.
Provide a conventional chapter index even if illustrated landmarks also act as destinations; order in the DOM remains understandable without the art.
styles.typography: Use a reading face with enough character to belong to the drawings, plus limited display lettering for scene titles. Hand-lettered art needs equivalent real text. Captions, controls and errors use stable, readable type, with no text embedded only in raster illustrations.
styles.material: Build an asset bible: line weight, perspective, palette, texture, recurring objects and prohibited inconsistencies. Rinpa offers a studied example of motif rhythm and open fields, not a license to flatten a Japanese tradition into a generic decorative style or reuse museum imagery.
styles.motion: A restrained environmental change can respond to a deliberate action or completed chapter. Keep background activity pausable and nonessential; reduced motion shows the same narrative information in stills.
styles.interaction: Illustrated landmarks have visible names and ordinary link equivalents. Tooltips are supplementary; help, skip and return routes remain obvious. Delight confirms actual progress and never fabricates achievements.
styles.mobile: Author a portrait crop or simplified scene with the same key motif, then place content in a clean vertical sequence. Do not miniaturize the whole landscape and make visitors hunt for tiny targets.
styles.use_when: The project can sustain original illustration and a specific narrative world, such as a learning journey, cultural story or unusually tangible product explanation.
styles.avoid_when: A stock illustration pack is doing all the identity work, art delays core tasks, or the world cannot remain coherent across recovery and utility screens.
styles.signature: A subject-specific motif changes meaning across overview, specimen and completion without changing its visual grammar.

styles.name: Spatial Technical / The Exploded Model
styles.thesis: Use space to explain a real system—layers, dependencies, scale or assembly—while keeping the controls and the equivalent explanation on an ordinary accessible plane.
composition: Give one system model a generous stage and a nearby explanation rail; anchor the title, current layer and primary task outside the model.
Explode or section the subject along a meaningful axis, with persistent labels connecting each visible part to its role.
Follow the overview with two-dimensional section diagrams and a factual specification ledger; not every page needs a live three-dimensional object.
Keep navigation and control positions stable while the model changes. Decorative perspective must not turn text and hit areas into skewed surfaces.
styles.typography: Use a clear technical sans, distinguish quantities from labels through alignment and weight, and reserve monospace for meaningful units or IDs. Model annotations should retain practical screen size at zoom; dense specifications use tabular numerals with explicit units.
styles.material: An original vector, CSS, SVG or lightweight 3D model based on the actual system. Show real part relationships and scale honestly. Provide a static section image and text legend before optional heavy rendering loads.
styles.motion: User-triggered layer separation explains assembly; provide reset, named views and a static equivalent. Avoid automatic camera orbit. Reduced motion switches views without camera travel, and low-power devices retain the essential diagram.
styles.interaction: Named part buttons and a keyboard-accessible layer list match pointer selection. Drag/orbit is optional; selected part and associated explanation are visible in text, and deep links can identify a layer when useful.
styles.mobile: Replace the full model with section views and labeled next/previous or part controls. Put the explanation directly below the selected view; never require a two-finger gesture to access basic content.
styles.use_when: Spatial relationships genuinely explain the offering, infrastructure, physical object or workflow, and the team can provide an accurate model.
styles.avoid_when: A floating abstract object stands in for missing product explanation, 3D is required to navigate, or performance and accessibility fallbacks are unfunded.
styles.signature: Selecting a named layer exposes the matching section and explanation, making spatial depth an explanatory operation rather than a visual effect.

styles.name: Expressive Material / The Transforming Surface
styles.thesis: Give a digital surface one convincing material behavior tied to the subject, then use that behavior sparingly to make hierarchy and state tangible.
composition: Start with a product-specific specimen—fabric, liquid, light, folded paper or a digital artifact—and a direct statement of the task or offer.
Choose one governing behavior such as folding, refraction or pooling. Use it for the focal artifact and a small number of meaningful transitions, not as texture on every component.
Pair expressive regions with calm functional regions whose controls, prices and labels remain perfectly ordinary to use.
Vary silhouette, scale and edge treatment around the same material rule; let content hierarchy decide where a bounded panel is actually needed.
styles.typography: Choose type that has a deliberate relationship to the material—crisp against soft, or broad against fine—without sacrificing text readability. Keep normal prose and controls on an opaque, stable plane. Display type can interact with the specimen; required labels cannot refract, blur or melt.
styles.material: Original macro photography, scans, vector simulations or lightweight shaders. Glass, gradients, gloss and purple are available materials and colors, not universal defaults or bans. Name their role and test the actual background composites before using them beneath text.
styles.motion: Make the chosen material respond to one meaningful action with a bounded transition. No endless simulation behind a form. Reduced motion uses a strong still specimen and direct fill, outline or label changes.
styles.interaction: Material behavior reinforces actual selected, expanded or completed states; it never substitutes for semantic state or clear controls. Focus is stable and high visibility, and actions remain usable when effects fail or scripting is unavailable.
styles.mobile: Use a pre-rendered or simplified specimen when live effects cost too much. Recompose the expressive field above or beside the action rather than hiding all personality; preserve clear touch targets and readable contrast.
styles.use_when: The subject has a distinctive material or transformation, and the team can maintain the effect with credible assets and a real performance fallback.
styles.avoid_when: Effects hide an absent thesis, visual layers prevent reliable contrast, or a repeated task would be slowed by a showpiece interaction.
styles.signature: One material rule connects the opening specimen to a useful state transition, creating continuity without a catalog of unrelated effects.
